sections.text:
fix: migrate (not crash) when on-disk meta predates a Meta field
In exfer-stack/exfer-indexer, his own repository.
https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-indexer/pull/4

## The bug
Deploying v0.3.0 over a v0 index crash-looped:
```
storage error: decode meta: io error: unexpected end of file
```
`FollowerMeta` gained a `schema_version` field, so an old blob is a byte-**prefix** of the current layout. bincode (positional, non-self-describing) hits EOF decoding it, and `#[serde(default)]` does **not** recover it. Since the version can only be read by decoding the whole record, `Db::open` errored *before* the schema migration could run — so the careful from-genesis backfill never executed, and recovery needed a manual `mv index.redb`.

## The fix
In `migrate_schema`, treat an **undecodable-but-present** checkpoint as a legacy (v0) DB and run the existing from-genesis backfill instead of erroring. The index is derived/rebuildable, so reconstructing from genesis is a safe recovery; the backfill is non-destructive (idempotent apply — existing tables keep serving during the re-walk). No more crash-loop, no manual db move.

Also: corrects the now-wrong `#[serde(default)]` doc comment; adds a regression test (v0 blob → migrates to genesis + stamps version, stays migrated on reopen).

Gates: **fmt + clippy -D warnings + full test suite (27) green**, incl. the new `pre_versioning_meta_migrates_instead_of_crashing`.

> Clarifies the 'why reindex on restart' concern: a same-version restart does NOT reindex (resumes from checkpoint); only a schema bump does, and only to backfill new historical tables — now gracefully, without crashing or manual intervention.
